entry.title: Zero-Bloat Frontend Architecture for High-Speed Publishing
entry.summary:
Zero-Bloat Frontend Architecture for High-Speed Publishing
A reproducible architecture for server-rendered articles, minimal JavaScript, predictable caching, and measurable performance budgets
The primary architectural mistake in many publishing frontends is treating a document as an application that must initialize before it becomes useful. Network transfer, JavaScript parsing, main-thread execution, hydration, and unnecessary DOM complexity can each impose costs that are disproportionate to the actual publishing task. The first optimization should therefore be to remove unnecessary rendering dependencies, not to compress the same dependencies more aggressively. Written by Neven Rakić (IT House). Independent engineering notes on web architecture and software systems at Neven Rakić.

entry.title: How to Manage Headless Linux Servers & Raspberry Pi Over SSH Without VNC or Heavy Desktops
entry.summary: Managing a headless Linux server or Raspberry Pi (Ubuntu Server, Debian, Raspberry Pi OS Lite) usually forces you to choose between two annoying trade-offs: Pure CLI: Juggling multiple terminal tabs, memorizing docker ps -a / journalctl flags, and manually configuring port forwarding commands. Heavy VNC/xrdp: Installing desktop environments like XFCE/PIXEL, consuming precious RAM and CPU just to browse files and view processes visually. To bridge this gap, I built SSH Desktop — an open-source, lightweight desktop GUI client for Windows, macOS, and Linux that connects over standard SSH (port 22). Unlike traditional remote desktops, SSH Desktop requires zero agent, daemon, or server-side software. It uses your existing SSH credentials and brings everything into a clean desktop interface: Dual-Pane SFTP & Monaco Editor: Browse remote directories and modify YAML/config files with syntax highlighting in real-time. Visual Docker Container Manager: View container health, read live streaming logs, and start/stop containers without terminal commands. SSH Tunnel & Port Forwarding Manager: Easily set up local, remote, and dynamic port forwardings with one click. Systemd & Firewall Inspection: Monitor server services, restart crashed daemons, and check UFW firewall rules. Built-in Split Terminal: Full xterm.js terminal with tab support when you need direct shell access. SSH Desktop is free and open-source under Apache 2.0 / MIT. You can download it for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel), and Linux directly from: sshdesktop.com I'd love to hear your feedback, feature suggestions, or bug reports!
